_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); electric utility signals

pit_profile.why: The Southern Company: 'Southern Company owns all of the outstanding common stock of Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Gulf Power, and Mississippi Power, each of which is an operating public utility company. The traditional operating companies supply electric service in the states of Alabama, Georgia, Florida, and Mississippi.'; among its risk factors, 'Southern Company and its subsidiaries are subject to substantial governmental regulation.', 'The operating results of Southern Company, the traditional operating companies, and Southern Power are affected by weather conditions and may fluctuate on a seasonal and quarterly basis.' and 'The costs of compliance with current and future environmental laws, including laws and regulations designed to address air quality, water, coal combustion byproducts, global climate change, renewable energy standards, and other matters and the incurrence of environmental liabilities could negatively impact the net income, cash flows, and financial condition of Southern Company, the traditional operating companies, and/or Southern Power.' (its own FY2012 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an electric utility on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on climate change legislation stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS -2.1%/yr (worst year FY03-FY12, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +6.1%/yr (Q1 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +6.1%/yr (FY03-FY12 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +6.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY03-FY12); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: SO (retrospective, 2013-06-07) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 1.85x (19.0% downside to Bear $36 / +10.3% upside to Bull $49) | Adj composite 2.33 vs market 3.93: gap -1.60 [OVERVALUED] | +18% above the EPP floor $38 (14x FY13E $2.68) | Conservative 2-yr case: +7.4% total (+3.7%/yr) | At 16.6x FY13E the 15% hurdle price $59 sits above the BULL case; retail kWh sales +2.3% in Q1 2013, forward revenues +8.1% (no Q2 2013 revenue guide, Q1 2013 revenue as reported); no disruption theme is live for an electric utility on this date.
